s: A steel-clad museum rising beside Gdańsk's historic Shipyard Gate No. 2, built where the August 1980 strikes that founded Solidarity actually took place.
w: The building's rust-coloured, ship-hull façade was designed to echo the cranes and steel plating of the shipyard around it, standing directly beside Gate No. 2, through which striking workers passed in 1980. Inside, the permanent exhibition traces the Solidarity movement from the 1970 shipyard shootings through the 1980s underground to the 1989 Round Table talks, and holds Lech Wałęsa's Nobel Peace Prize medal.
_facts: Opened 2014 on the site of the former Lenin Shipyard
Entered via the historic Shipyard Gate No. 2
Holds Lech Wałęsa's 1983 Nobel Peace Prize medal

s: A bronze Neptune has presided over Gdańsk's Długi Targ since 1633, cast for a Baltic merchant city that wanted its own Poseidon.
w: Designed by Abraham van den Blocke and cast in bronze by Gerd Benning, the fountain took decades to assemble and was finally switched on in 1633 in front of Artus Court. It suffered heavy damage in WWII, was restored in 1954 and again fully in 2012. Local legend holds that a prankster once poured Goldwasser vodka into the basin, giving the drink its city nickname.
_facts: Designed by Abraham van den Blocke, cast by Gerd Benning
Stands in front of Artus Court on Długi Targ

q: St Mary's Basilica Krakow bugle call
s: Europe's largest brick Gothic church, where a five-note trumpet call has sounded hourly from the tower for centuries, breaking off mid-note in memory of a watchman killed mid-alarm.
w: St. Mary's anchors the northeast corner of Kraków's Main Market Square; its taller Hejnalica tower is reached by 239 narrow steps and has been staffed around the clock, traditionally by city firefighters, since medieval times. The hejnał mariacki is played four times an hour toward the cardinal points and always cuts off abruptly, commemorating a watchman said to have been shot mid-alarm. Inside, Veit Stoss's carved wooden altarpiece is unveiled with mechanical fanfare at noon.
_facts: Taller Hejnalica tower is 82m, 239 steps, no elevator
Hejnał mariacki bugle call played hourly, every day
Houses Veit Stoss's 13m wooden altarpiece (1477-1489)

s: A Renaissance trading hall splits Kraków's medieval square in two, its ground floor still selling wares as it has for over five centuries.
w: Sukiennice began as medieval stone stalls for the cloth trade and was rebuilt in its current Renaissance form after an 1555 fire, its delicate attic parapet and carved masks added by Italian architects. The ground-floor arcade still functions as a market; the upper floor holds the Sukiennice Gallery of 19th-century Polish painting, part of the National Museum.
_facts: Rebuilt in Renaissance style after an 1555 fire
Ground floor still functions as a trade market
Upper floor houses the Sukiennice Gallery (National Museum)

s: Warsaw's royal residence was dynamited by German sappers in 1944 and rebuilt from scratch between 1971 and 1988, financed almost entirely by public donations.
w: After the Warsaw Uprising, German demolition squads reduced the Castle to rubble as deliberate retribution. Reconstruction didn't begin until 1971, using salvaged fragments, pre-war measured drawings and Bernardo Bellotto's 18th-century cityscapes to rebuild the interiors; ordinary Poles funded much of the work through public collections. It now stands at the entrance to the Old Town on Castle Square.
_facts: Almost entirely destroyed by German forces in 1944
Reconstruction ran 1971-1988, funded largely by public donations
Rebuilt partly using 18th-century Canaletto paintings as reference

q: Rynek Starego Miasta Warsaw Old Town Market Square
s: Warsaw's oldest square was flattened by German demolition squads in 1944 and rebuilt from paintings and photographs so precisely that UNESCO still lists it as a World Heritage reconstruction.
w: Laid out in the late 13th century as the commercial heart of the newly founded city, the square was systematically dynamited after the 1944 Warsaw Uprising. Architects rebuilt it between 1948 and 1953 using pre-war photographs, Canaletto's cityscapes and surviving plans. At its centre stands the Warsaw Mermaid, a symbol drawn from the city's coat of arms.
_facts: Founded late 13th century; systematically destroyed in 1944
Rebuilt 1948-1953 using period paintings, photos and plans
Part of Warsaw's Old Town, UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980

s: A quiet meadow between three villages holds the field where the Polish-Lithuanian army broke the Teutonic Order in 1410, one of medieval Europe's largest battles.
w: On 15 July 1410, the combined forces of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeated the Teutonic Knights near Grunwald, Stębark and Łodwigowo, reshaping the balance of power in medieval Central Europe. An 8-metre granite obelisk was raised on the battlefield's high ground in 1960, flanked by eleven 30-metre flagpoles bearing the arms of the units that fought there. A museum pavilion opened in 2022 beneath the site's amphitheatre, and the battle is re-enacted there every July.
_facts: Battle fought 15 July 1410, Poland-Lithuania vs the Teutonic Order
Granite obelisk monument erected 1960
Museum of the Battle of Grunwald opened 2022

s: Fryderyk Chopin was born in this modest manor annexe on the banks of the Utrata River in 1810, and it has drawn pianists and pilgrims ever since.
w: The building is not a grand mansion but the surviving eastern outbuilding of a larger manor that no longer exists, given a columned porch in a 1930s renovation. Opened as a museum in 1949, the centenary of Chopin's death, it sits inside a 17-hectare park of specimen trees and hosts open-air piano recitals through the summer, on the edge of Kampinos National Park.
_facts: Chopin born here, 1810
Museum opened in 1949, the centenary of Chopin's death
Set within a 17-hectare park used for summer piano recitals

s: About 400 pines outside Gryfino bend sharply northward near their base before growing straight again, and nobody has ever definitively explained why.
w: Planted around 1930, roughly 400 Scots pines in this grove all curve into a J-shape close to ground level -- most bending north -- before rising vertically for the rest of their height. Theories range from a deliberate technique for pre-bending timber, interrupted by WWII, to snow damage or an unexplained local anomaly, but none has been proven. Free to enter and unfenced, the grove sits a few kilometres outside Gryfino, facing Germany across the Oder.
_facts: Roughly 400 pine trees, all planted around 1930
Trunks bend sharply near the base, mostly northward, then grow straight
Leading theory: deliberate tree-shaping for curved timber, interrupted by WWII

n: John Paul II Family Home Museum
q: Dom Rodzinny Jana Pawla II Wadowice
s: Karol Wojtyła was born in this apartment building on Wadowice's market square in 1920, and it now traces his path from small-town childhood to the papacy.
w: The museum occupies the actual tenement flat where the future Pope John Paul II was born and spent his early years, next to the Basilica of the Presentation of the Virgin Mary where his father took him to daily Mass. Exhibits move from Wojtyła family possessions and school records through his wartime years and priesthood to his 1978 election and 2014 canonisation. Downstairs, a bakery still sells kremówka, the cream cake tied to the Pope's own local nostalgia.
_facts: Museum has operated since 1984 in the family's original apartment
Beside the Basilica of the Presentation of Mary
Traces Karol Wojtyła's life from birth (1920) through 2014 canonisation
